newsitem.title: FRANCE: France's EDF to go ahead with reduced hours pact.
newsitem.headline: France's EDF to go ahead with reduced hours pact.

text.p: The chairman of utility Electricite de France, Edmond Alphandery, said on Tuesday that EDF would implement an accord to reduce working hours despite the opposition of two unions.
"We will apply it. I'm confident," Alphandery told Europe 1 radio. "This innovative accord for jobs has been signed by three of the five unions at Electricite de France-Gaz de France."
The CFDT, CFTC and CGC unions signed the accord last Friday, but the biggest union at the utility, the CGT, and the centrist FO oppose it.

The accord envisages a reduction in the work week to 32 hours from 38 except for the lowest paid positions and more flexible work hours to accommodate customers. In exchange, EDF has agreed to hire 15,000 young workers over three years.
